title: Mega Man Zero 3
collection: Mega Man Zero/ZX Legacy Collection · GBA
intro: A mission route with the health upgrades, Sub Tanks, equipment and rank decisions explained before you need them.
primer: Zero 3 removes weapon-level grinding: charged attacks and Saber combos are ready from the start. Recoil Rod replaces Chain Rod; its charged downward strike launches Zero upward from ground or suitable enemies. At the base, speak to Cerveau after the introduction to receive Recoil Rod and Shield Boomerang.

Chips equip separately on the head, body and feet. Body element chips change charged attacks. Two Satellite elf slots provide reusable support without a rank penalty. Fusion elves are consumed and still lower scores; two of them become the extra Sub Tanks.

EX Skills still require A/S when entering the mission. Entering Cyberspace makes a stage easier and activates many elf effects, but penalizes the mission score and prevents enemy disk drops. Keep rank runs and collection runs on separate saves.

Take Secret Disks to Cerveau for analysis. A disk in your inventory is not yet an equipped chip or raised elf. Zero 3’s optional modification cards are available through the collection; check the card menu rather than following obsolete e-Reader hardware instructions.
routeIntro: Devilbat supplies Thunder for Flizard; Flame then handles Childre. Finish Mantisk and the fixed Missile Factory intermission. Collect Elphy at the base before Copy X. Follow the second and final mission groups, returning with Flame or Double Jump for missed equipment.

warning.title: Keep Satellite and Fusion elves separate.
warning.text: Satellite support does not lower rank. Consuming Fusion elves and entering Cyberspace do. Collect Elphy in base room 02D after Missile Factory and before Copy X; that base disk is time-sensitive.

returns.title: Auto-Charge with Flame; retry the tank with Double Jump

returnIntro: Revisit cleared areas from the base for equipment and supplies. Keep a separate save before a one-time mission or the final assault.
completionText: All three head chips, five body rewards, seven foot options, two physical tanks and Artan/Zictan if using Fusion tanks. Check the twelve EX rewards separately; 200 disks are the optional full collection.

sections.title: Final assault
paragraphs: Complete Sub Arcadia, then the rematches. Elemental bosses retain their weaknesses; neutral charged Saber works on Mantisk and Kelverian.
Omega’s early forms have exposed targets between large attacks. Use charged Saber/Buster and leave space to read the next pattern.
Against the final humanoid form, attack during recovery, retreat before his Saber combo, and use filled tanks from the menu. Preserve your endgame save before writing clear-game data.

sections.title: Secret Disks and modification cards
paragraphs: Equipment disks 001–006 and the health/tank disks are listed at their mission stops. The other disks include temporary elves, data and enemy records; there are 200 altogether.

Enemy disks often require several kills of a specific enemy and cannot drop in Cyberspace. Return in the ordinary world to collect them. Use the referenced numbered disk database for an optional full-library run.
Collection modification cards change specific effects. They are optional aids; the main route here assumes they are disabled.

sections.title: Useful tips
paragraphs: Raise a health elf and use it as a Satellite to gain support without consuming it. Only two Satellite effects can run at once, so choose for the next stage.
Recoil Rod bounces and the later Double Jump make Old Residential’s high tank much easier. You do not need to take repeated risky jumps on your first visit.
